text: James Luke Prendergast (April 7, 1800 – May 13, 1895) was a merchant and political figure in Newfoundland. He served in the Newfoundland and Labrador House of Assembly, representing Conception Bay from 1842 to 1852, Harbour Grace from 1855 to 1859, and again from 1860 to 1861 as a Liberal. Born in Harbour Grace, he was the son of James Prendergast and married Margaret Bransfield in 1825. In an 1840 by-election, he ran as an independent Liberal against Edmund Hanrahan, but due to widespread violence during the campaign, Governor Henry Prescott invalidated the election results. Prendergast was first elected as a Liberal in 1842. He was defeated when he ran again as an independent Liberal in 1852. In 1855, after being elected as a Liberal, he served as acting superintendent of fisheries. His 1859 election was overturned, but he was elected in the subsequent 1860 by-election. The general election in Harbour Grace in 1861 did not open the polls due to the threat of violence, and Prendergast was defeated in a later by-election that year. He ran unsuccessfully for a seat in 1869 as an anti-Confederate. Later in life, he served as sheriff of Harbour Grace and as a justice of the peace. He died in Harbour Grace at the age of 95.
